name: Dunkaroos
blurb: General Mills' cookies-and-frosting snack pack, gone from the US in 2012, back in 2020
title: Dunkaroos: What Happened to Them and Are They Back?
description: Dunkaroos are General Mills' little cookies with a tub of frosting for dunking, a 1990s lunchbox snack. They left US shelves in 2012 and came back in 2020.
answer: Dunkaroos are a General Mills snack pack of small cookies with a well of frosting to dunk them in, introduced in the early 1990s (General Mills dates them to 1992) with a kangaroo mascot. They were discontinued in the United States in 2012 but kept selling in Canada for some years after. General Mills brought them back to US stores in summer 2020, and they are still made, with occasional limited flavors.

body: A Dunkaroos pack is a small plastic tray split in two: one side holds about ten bite-sized cookies, the other a scoop of frosting roughly a cubic inch in size. You dunk each cookie in the frosting and eat it. The name is a mix of "dunk" and "kangaroos", and the brand leaned on an Australian theme, with kangaroo mascots and cookies shaped like circles stamped with a D, feet or the mascot.

The original mascot was Sydney the Kangaroo. A 1996 contest replaced him with Duncan, billed as the "dunkin' daredevil". Over the years the packs came as graham cookies with chocolate or vanilla frosting, vanilla cookies with vanilla frosting and rainbow sprinkles, strawberry frosting and other mixes; General Mills says four new frosting flavors, including cinnamon and peanut butter, arrived in 1993.

sections.h: Why they disappeared and came back
body: General Mills did not give a detailed public reason for pulling Dunkaroos in the US in 2012. What kept the brand alive was the gap between the two countries: Canadians could still buy them, Americans who grew up with them could not, and the company played on that with its 2016 Smugglaroos campaign.

The 2020 return was teased on social media that January and announced on February 3. The new pack is larger, 1.5 ounces instead of 1 ounce, with noticeably less sugar according to the company, and it uses only the round D-stamped cookie. A separate run in Australia, made by Nestlé with chocolate-hazelnut frosting, appeared in late 2019 and was dropped again in 2020.

faq.a: Not any more. They were dropped in the US in 2012 but returned in 2020 and are still sold, with limited editions from time to time.
In the early 1990s. General Mills dates the launch to 1992; some sources say 1990.

faq.q: Are the new Dunkaroos the same as the old ones?
faq.a: Close, but not identical. The 2020 pack is bigger, has less sugar according to General Mills and uses one cookie shape instead of several.
